courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Undergraduate Open Seminar
courses.description: Approved for letter and S/U grading. May be repeated in the same term up to 6 hours, if topics vary; May be repeated in separate terms up to 12 hours, if topics vary.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Basic Constitutional Law & Individual Rights
courses.description: An introduction to the main themes of the American Constitution - with an emphasis on the First and Fourteenth Amendments - and to basic techniques of constitutional interpretation. Attention will be paid to the interplay of constitutional text, judicial doctrine, and constitutional decision-making outside the judiciary. No prerequisites.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Introduction to Law
courses.description: Guides the undergraduate student in an initial study of law and legal reasoning. Covers the nature and function of rules/law, the distinctiveness of legal reasoning, and the way in which law responds to social phenomena and contributes to the development of different social, business and economic institutions. Includes both criminal and civil proceedings. Serves as a general foundation course for those interested in applying to law school. Also of interest to students who are not interested in pursuing a more formal law education, but for whom general legal training will enhance their career aspirations. Develops skills that are transferable to virtually any career.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Transitional Justice
courses.description: Wrongdoing is part of the history of many, if not most, political communities around the globe. This course examines the moral questions that dealing with past wrongdoing raise. Our focus is specifically on political wrongdoing, that is, wrongdoing inflicted on individuals by the state or groups contesting the state. Such wrongdoing has taken different forms, from slavery, to forced disappearances, to programs of torture and of land appropriation. We also focus on two specific political contexts: the United States and South Africa. In this course, we survey a range of legal measures including criminal punishment, truth commissions, reparations, and apology, that have been, and can be used, to deal with legacies of wrongdoing. Not available for Graduate or Professional credit.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Living the Law
courses.description: Combines the study of major areas of law with small-group simulations to explore how the law operates in different contexts in American society. Students interested in experiencing how lawyers, lawmakers, prosecutors, and judges work with the law will benefit from this course. Substantively, the class surveys the roots of American law; the creation of the United States Constitution; the evolution of equal protection and due process law; and provides an overview of Contracts, Torts, Criminal Law, Family Law, and legal ethics and procedure.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Introduction to Legal Research
courses.description: Introduction to tools and techniques essential for legal practice and scholarship. Students will be able to identify legal issues and relevant facts from a fact pattern, devise a research strategy, find and identify relevant legal information using free and proprietary sources, identify legal rules and principles from a series of authorities, and write a plain-English summary of findings that includes an explanation of the relevant rules. Approved for Letter and S/U grading.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Art and Cultural Property Law
courses.description: This course concerns the emergence of "art" and "cultural property" law as a distinct field of legal inquiry and practice. Still, this subject draws from nearly the entire spectrum of traditional legal subjects – intellectual property, free speech, contracts, crime, treaties, tax, etc. Art and Cultural Property Law deals with the relationships, rights, transactions and disputes among collectors, artists (and their heirs), dealers, auction houses, museums and other art world participants (including local and foreign governments, sovereign nations and indigenous peoples, the entertainment industry, sports franchises and social media). Among the dozens of important relevant issues in this field are the successes and failures of law in policing cultural heritage crimes, the rise of artistic nationalism, cultural heritage as a casualty of war, censorship, and provenance studies. Approved for Letter and S/U grading.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: The Operation of the American Criminal Justice System
courses.description: Guides undergraduates to a deeper understanding of the operation of the justice system through bi-weekly field trips to see court proceedings paired with in-class discussions on the alternate weeks. Focusing on criminal law, students learn how the state and federal systems differ; how law enforcement personnel, investigators, judges, attorneys, and other legal professionals serve the system; and how cases are processed. Students will also explore a variety of controversies that have plagued the justice system through the years.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Law and Literature
courses.description: Literary and cultural texts will offer students context for understanding how legal systems differ from one another and over time, revealing how moral, ethical and political realities reflected in literature motivate and illuminate the law, as well as issues arising from its application, the role of lawyers in society, and major legal doctrines spanning both criminal and civil law. Students will read and respond primarily to literary texts, supplemented by legal documents and abridged passages from interdisciplinary scholarship.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: LAW Study Abroad
courses.description: Provides campus credit for study at accredited foreign institutions or approved overseas programs. Final determination of credit granted is made after the student's successful completion of work. No undergraduate credit. 0 to 18 graduate hours. Approved for Letter and S/U grading.
courses.prereqText: Full academic standing in the College of Law or Graduate College; consent of major department. Law students, successful completion of the first year's requirements.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: LLM Legal Writing and Research
courses.description: Designed and developed to equip incoming LL.M students with the necessary background in U.S. constitutional law, legal research, analysis, and writing for effective classroom performance. Approved for S/U grading only.
courses.prereqText: Admission to the U.S. LLM program.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Professional Responsibility
courses.description: This course concerns itself with the laws, regulations, and customs that govern the legal profession in the United States, and considers those matters in the context of an increasingly globalized legal profession. Students will be expected to attend class, review the assigned reading before class, participate in class discussions and exercises, complete written assignments, and examinations.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Introduction to the Law for Graduate Students
courses.description: Offers foundational principles and structures of the American legal system, essential for working professionals in business, technology, and government who interact with the law and legal regulations. Surveys key substantive areas—including constitutional, criminal, tort, contract, property, and family law—alongside civil and criminal procedures. Through case studies, participants analyze law’s interplay with societal shifts, applying foundational legal concepts to enhance compliance, risk management, strategic planning, and ethical decision-making for career advancement.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to graduate students in the College of Law.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Legal Reasoning for Graduate Students
courses.description: Non-lawyers in business, tech, and government gain foundational legal reasoning skills to evaluate and integrate legal advice in strategic decision-making. Tailored to working professionals, the course emphasizes principles to empower constructive, strategic interactions with legal counsel and other legal actors, and applying concepts like sources of law, remedies, and compliance strategies through case studies.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to graduate students in the College of Law.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Computer Literacy for Graduate Students
courses.description: Equips non-lawyers with foundational computing knowledge—from hardware and algorithms to networks and AI—while exploring legal implications like data privacy, cybersecurity regulations, intellectual property, and ethical governance. Through case studies, participants apply basic computing concepts to a variety of real life scenarios to enhance compliance, risk mitigation, and strategic innovation in business, technology, and government contexts. Students acquire the basic computer literacy needed to navigate legal frameworks in ways critical for professionals navigating digital and contemporary business landscapes.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to graduate students in the College of Law.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Working Effectively with Lawyers-Grads
courses.description: Introduces non-lawyer professionals to the fundamentals of working effectively with lawyers. Topics covered include the foundations of the practice of law and unauthorized practice of law; best practices with respect to the use of the Internet for legal research; finding and analyzing cases; finding and analyzing statutes and regulations; finding and analyzing secondary sources; reviewing and organizing contracts; analyzing laws and synthesizing facts; communicating effectively with legal counsel; writing persuasively, accurately, and clearly; and utilizing artificial intelligence (AI) thoughtfully and responsibly in a legal environment.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to graduate students in the College of Law.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Ethics and Compliance for Graduate Students
courses.description: Explores ethical codes and compliance standards (e.g., FCPA, Sarbanes-Oxley) to foster organizational integrity. While learning legal compliance frameworks, students apply those frameworks to bribery or conflict-of-interest scenarios, analyze ethical lapses, and create training plans, preparing to advise on compliance strategies in fields like business, tech, and related fields.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to graduate students in the College of Law.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Corporate Governance for Graduate Students
courses.description: Covers corporate governance structures (e.g., fiduciary duties, shareholder rights) and their balance with business objectives. Students apply principles to board resolutions, analyze governance failures, and evaluate reforms, preparing to advise on corporate accountability in fields like business, tech, and related fields.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to graduate students in the College of Law.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Supply Chain Oversight for Graduate Students
courses.description: Addresses transparency standards (e.g., TVPRA) for ethical sourcing and vendor accountability. With a stronger understanding of governing legal frameworks, students learn to apply audit tools to global supply chains, analyze oversight gaps, and create compliance plans, preparing to manage supply chain risks.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to graduate students in the College of Law.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Antitrust Law for Graduate Students
courses.description: Explores antitrust reasoning and its application to violations like price-fixing or monopolization. Students analyze scenarios, evaluate compliance programs, and create strategies aligned with tech and governance, preparing to advise on competitive practices in business, tech, and related industries.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to graduate students in the College of Law.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Securities Law for Graduate Students
courses.description: Covers securities regulations (e.g., SEC disclosure rules) for investor protection and capital markets. Students apply compliance protocols, analyze disclosure failures, and create strategies, preparing to support financial compliance roles in in fields like business, tech, and related fields.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to graduate students in the College of Law.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Business Organizations for Graduate Students
courses.description: Examines business entity types (e.g., LLCs, corporations) and their governance/tax implications. Students apply entity selection, analyze dissolution risks, and evaluate hybrid structures, preparing to advise on business formation changes or strategies in fields like business, tech, and related fields.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to graduate students in the College of Law.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Employment Discrimination for Graduate Students
courses.description: Covers discrimination laws (e.g., Title VII, ADA) and their application to workplace equity. Mid-career professionals learn these legal frameworks and engage in practical applications and simulations, relevant to work in their industries, such as investigating harassment complaints, evaluating diversity initiatives, preparing to advise on inclusive HR practices.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to graduate students in the College of Law.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Individual Employee Rights for Graduate Students
courses.description: Explores statutory protections (e.g., FLSA, NLRA) and employee safeguards. Students apply termination guidelines and evaluate accommodations, preparing to manage employee relations compliance, with special application to mid-career professionals in business, tech, and related fields.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to graduate students in the College of Law.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Employee Benefits for Graduate Students
courses.description: Addresses legal requirements, connected to employment, for things like pensions and health plans. In addition to learning governing legal frameworks, students engage in practical applications, relevant to their industries in business, tech, and related fields, such as designing benefits plans, analyzing fiduciary duties, and creating and reviewing compliant policies, and preparing to support HR retention strategies.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to graduate students in the College of Law.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: AI Governance and Compliance for Graduate Students
courses.description: Covers AI regulations (e.g., EU AI Act) and compliance pathways. In addition to learning basic legal frameworks, students engage in practical applications relevant to mid-career work in business and tech, such as assessing AI tool deployments, evaluating audit outcomes, and preparing to advise on regulatory compliance.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to graduate students in the College of Law.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: AI and Data Privacy for Graduate Students
courses.description: Explores privacy laws (e.g., GDPR, CCPA) and their application to AI data flows. In addition to learning these legal frameworks, students apply this legal knowledge to case studies that are relevant to mid-career advancement in business, tech, and related fields, by engaging in activities such as conducting privacy assessments, evaluating anonymization, and preparing to manage AI-driven privacy risks.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to graduate students in the College of Law.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: AI Ethics & Bias for Graduate Students
courses.description: Addresses ethical guidelines and bias in AI models. In addition to learning these legal and policy frameworks, students apply them to activities that are common for mid-career professionals in business, tech, and related industries through case studies that ask them to do things such as debias AI methods, evaluate AI frameworks, and prepare recommendations to ensure equitable AI deployments.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to graduate students in the College of Law.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Cyberthreats and Compliance for Graduate Students
courses.description: Covers the laws relating to cyber threats (e.g., ransomware, malware, phishing, security breaches) and compliance obligations (e.g., NIST). In addition to learning the classes of possible threats and governing legal frameworks, students apply this knowledge to a variety of practical settings that are relevant to mid-career advancement in business, tech, and related fields, such as by modeling threats create or reviewing compliance plans, and preparing to advise on cybersecurity regulations.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to graduate students in the College of Law.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Cyber Risk Mitigation for Graduate Students
courses.description: Explores cyber risk controls (e.g., zero-trust architectures), insurance policies, and other mechanisms to mitigate cyber risks in light of legal standards. In addition learning about relevant legal standards for cyber risk mitigation, students apply that knowledge through cases studies to build skills relevant to mid-career development in business, tech, and related areas, such as developing remediation plans, evaluating mitigations, reviewing insurance provider agreements, and preparing to manage cyber risks in tech ecosystems.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to graduate students in the College of Law.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Cyber Incident Response for Graduate Students
courses.description: Addresses cyber incident response phases (e.g., NIST IR lifecycle). In addition to learning governing legal standards, disclosure requirements, and processes, students apply that knowledge to common problems faces by mid-career professionals in business, tech, and related industries through case studies that involve things like create response strategies, reviewing disclosures, and preparing to manage cyber incidents.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to graduate students in the College of Law.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Intellectual Property of Emerging Tech for Graduate Students
courses.description: Covers intellectual property regimes (e.g., AI patents, patents in fintech, patents in genomic methods) for emerging tech. In addition to learning the legal frameworks that govern these issues, students apply this knowledge to common problems that arise in mid-career business, tech, and related roles such as applying licensing strategies, creating protection plans, and preparing to advise on tech commercialization.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to graduate students in the College of Law.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Health Tech Law & Privacy for Graduate Students
courses.description: Explores legal regulations for health tech privacy, safety, and approval (e.g., HIPAA and FDA regulations) relevant to biotech, health, and medicine. In addition to learning about these legal frameworks, students will apply this legal knowledge to case studies that present problems common for mid-career professionals in business, tech, and medical industries such as applications of consent models, the creation and review of health privacy policies, and preparation to manage health tech compliance.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to graduate students in the College of Law.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Frontiers of Technology Law for Graduate Students
courses.description: Addresses legal frameworks and policies that govern emerging technologies (e.g., quantum export controls, fintech like blockchain) in novel or speculative tech. In additional to learning about the governing legal frameworks, students apply that knowledge to emerging technologies through case studies that are relevant to business, tech, and related industries by doing things like applying foresight tools, reviewing policy briefs, and preparing to advocate for adaptive regulations.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to graduate students in the College of Law.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Law Partner Scholar Notation
courses.description: Illinois Law Partner Scholars Program requirements provide designated students an opportunity to enhance their professional and personal competences in four areas: cultural awareness, leadership and team-building, academic excellence, and community involvement. The activities and contributions of designated students will advance the development of global law practice skills within the College of Law: 1) by providing points of comparison and contrast to U.S. Law; and 2) by understanding the social and business context of law outside the U.S. Approved for S/U grading only.
courses.prereqText: For students who are identified by Illinois Law Partner schools for admission into the Illinois LL.M. program.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Thesis Research
courses.description: Approved for S/U grading only.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Pro Bono Service
courses.description: Course carries no academic credit, but recognizes law students who provide at least sixty hours of pro bono legal service to the community. The sixty hours of service may be performed at any time during the student's three years of law school, and must be documented through reports to the Associate Dean for Academic Affairs. 0 graduate hours. 0 professional hours. Approved for S/U grading only. Students may enroll only with permission of the Associate Dean for Academic Affairs.
courses.prereqText: Enrollment in the J.D. or LL.M. program at the College of Law.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Contracts
courses.description: Enforceability of promises including unjust enrichment and reliance, offer and acceptance, mistake, unfairness and overreaching, unconscionability, Statute of Frauds, interpretation of contract language, conditions, and third party beneficiaries. 4 graduate hours. 4 professional hours.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Property
courses.description: Basic first-year course in property law, required of all students. Provides an overview of law of the land, with incidental coverage of personal property; includes the concept of property, acquisition of private property, recognized property interests, and gratuitous transfer of property interests. 4 graduate hours. 4 professional hours.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Torts
courses.description: Basic course in civil wrongs, including intentional torts (such as assault and battery), negligence (duty, unreasonable risk analysis, actual and proximate cause), and strict liability. 4 graduate hours. 4 professional hours.
courses.prereqText: Law students only.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Criminal Law
courses.description: Sources and purposes of the criminal law; the meaning of criminal responsibility; and the characteristics of particular crimes. 4 graduate hours. 4 professional hours.
courses.prereqText: Law students only.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Criminal Proc: Investigation
courses.description: Problems in the administration of criminal justice with emphasis on right to counsel, arrest, search, interrogation, lineups, and the scope and administration of exclusionary rules. 4 graduate hours. 3 professional hours.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Constitutional Law I
courses.description: Basic first-year course provides an introduction to constitutional law, including the origins of judicial review, basic Article III limits on federal court jurisdiction, the nature and scope of federal legislative power, the Commerce Clause, and the relationship of the federal government to the states. 4 graduate hours. 4 professional hours.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Civil Procedure
courses.description: Role and importance of procedure in litigation, including jurisdiction, pleadings and parties, pretrial motions and discovery, trial practice (except evidence), relationship between judge and jury, the effect of a decision in one case on subsequent litigation between the same or different parties (res judicata), verdicts and judgements, and appelate review. 4 graduate hours. 4 professional hours.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Legal Writing & Analysis
courses.description: Emphasis on development and improvement of skills in legal writing, and training in legal bibliography. Assignments may include brief writing and preparation of legal memoranda and opinions. 3 graduate hours. 2 professional hours.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Introduction to Advocacy
courses.description: Continuation of LAW 609. Introduction to Advocacy is required in the second semester of the first year for further development of legal research skills persuasive writing and oral advocacy. Each student will work on the preparation of a summary judgment motion and an appellate brief relating to their first semester assignment, then argue their assigned case before a panel of local attorneys and faculty. 2 graduate hours. 3 professional hours. Approved for Letter and S/U grading.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Constitutional Law III
courses.description: This elective for second-and third-year law students is an intensive study of the First Amendment to the Constitution and its application to the states through the Fourteenth Amendment. Examines decisions of the U.S. Supreme Court in areas concerning freedom of speech, religion, and the press. Specific topics include punishment of criminal advocacy; regulation of picketing and public demonstrations; obscenity; commercial speech; regulation of news media; and religious exemptions from government regulation. 4 graduate hours. 3 professional hours.
courses.prereqText: LAW 606.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Administrative Law
courses.description: Functions of administrative tribunals in federal, state, and municipal government; the procedure before such administrative tribunals; and judicial relief from administrative decisions. 4 graduate hours. 3 professional hours.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Environmental Law and Pol I
courses.description: Course is the basic introduction to Environment Law; it considers the principal legal approaches used to deal with environmental problems, including common-law, statutory, regulatory, and economic-incentive systems. 4 graduate hours. 3 professional hours.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Natural Resources
courses.description: Legal problems associated with the ownership and use of land, water, and mineral resources. 2 or 4 graduate hours. 3 professional hours.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Wildlife Law
courses.description: Covers a variety of legal issues relating to the status and treatment of wildlife and the management of natural areas for the conservation of biodiversity. 4 graduate hours. 3 professional hours.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Health Law Policy
courses.description: This course focuses on the profound legal and policy issues raised by changes in health law and the U.S. health care delivery system including: access to health law and the U.S. health care delivery system including: access to health services; the financing and organization of the health care system; development of legal standards to ensure quality of care; and issues of long-term care. In addition, we will focus on the process of making laws and polices; what entities, institutions, and individuals control decisions about the quality and cost of health care. We will also explore the need and basis for reform. 4 graduate hours. 3 professional hours.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Land Use Planning
courses.description: Examination of the legal and administrative aspects of land development and regulation in an urban society, including the techniques and problems of planning; the tools of plan effectuation, such as zoning, subdivision regulation, renewal and redevelopment, and housing programs; and the allocation of decision-making among various levels of government. 2 to 4 graduate hours. 2 to 3 professional hours.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Real Estate Finance
courses.description: Methods of financing land acquisition and residential and commercial development, including publicly owned and subsidized housing. 4 graduate hours. 3 professional hours.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: State and Local Government
courses.description: The law governing the structure, powers, and operation of local governments in urban and suburban areas with analysis of political, economic, and social implications. 4 graduate hours. 3 professional hours.
courses.prereqText: LAW 606.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Legal Research
courses.description: Introduction to the basic tools and methodology used in conducting legal research and will develop the skills necessary to identify and locate relevant, complete and current legal information in both print and digital formats. Weekly problem-based research exercises will be assigned. 1 graduate hour. 1 or 2 professional hours. Approved for letter and S/U grading. Required in the first year, fall term.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Bankruptcy
courses.description: Study of the regulation of the relationship between debtors and creditors under the federal Bankruptcy Code. 4 graduate hours. 3 or 4 professional hours.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Secured Transactions
courses.description: Study of secured transactions under Article 9 of the Uniform Commercial Code. 2 to 4 graduate hours. 2 to 3 professional hours.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Business Associations I
courses.description: Examines the basic legal consequences for individuals, organizations, and society of the formation, control, and financing of organizations. Surveys agency relationships, partnerships, and close and public corporations. 4 graduate hours. 3 or 4 professional hours.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Securities Regulation
courses.description: Explores the federal securities laws governing issuance of securities in the primary markets. Emphasis on regulatory requirements governing corporate financing. 4 graduate hours. 3 professional hours.
courses.prereqText: LAW 633.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Securities Litigation
courses.description: Focuses in detail on the substantive law and strategic considerations that are important in securities litigation, whether private suits by individual investors, private class actions under federal securities laws, or federal and state government enforcement proceedings. Topics include: 10(b) fraud suits under the 1934 Act, 11 and 12(a)(2) suits under the 1933 Act, insider trader liability, procedural issues in class actions, and litigation under federal proxy solicitation and tender offer regulations. 4 graduate hours. 3 professional hours.
courses.prereqText: LAW 633.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Business Associations II
courses.description: The second course in the sequence. Covers derivative suits, corporate finance, introduction to securities regulation, insider trading and mergers and acquisitions. 4 graduate hours. 3 professional hours.
courses.prereqText: LAW 633.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: White Collar Crime
courses.description: This course will focus on the federal statutes commonly invoked in corporate and white collar prosecutions, including those used in prosecutions for conspiracy, mail and wire fraud, RICO, extortion, bribery, tax offenses, obstruction of justice, and false statements. The class will investigate the theoretical and policy framework for individual and institutional responsibility in our criminal justice system and will also explore emerging theories of corporate criminal liability and the principles undergirding the sanctions imposed for white collar crime. 3 to 4 graduate hours. 2 to 4 professional hours. Approved for Letter and S/U grading.
courses.prereqText: This course is appropriate for law students who have completed introductory courses in criminal law and procedure. Some students have found it helpful to complete the course in LAW 633 before taking this course, but it is not a prerequisite.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Corporate Finance
courses.description: Analysis of corporate and securities law problems using the tools of modern financial theory. Emphases will typically include valuation, capital structure, and fundamental changes of public corporations. 4 graduate hours. 3 professional hours.
courses.prereqText: LAW 633.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Antitrust Law
courses.description: The limitations imposed by the Sherman Act, Clayton Act, and Federal Trade Commission Act on anticompetitive practices by business firms; emphasizes price fixing and other agreements among competitors, monopolization, mergers, exclusive dealing, tying arrangements. Considers applicability of traditional rules to intellectual property and new technologies. 4 graduate hours. 3 professional hours.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Trademark & Unfair Competition
courses.description: Course introduces basic legal concepts relating to statutory and common-law trademark, interference with contractual relations and trade libel, the federalization of unfair competition law, and the role of the Federal Trade Commission in consumer protection activities. 4 graduate hours. 3 professional hours.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Copyright Law
courses.description: Offers an in-depth look at the legal aspects of copyright with special emphasis on the application of traditional copyright principles to new technologies and media of expression. 4 graduate hours. 3 professional hours.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Patent Law
courses.description: Historical development of protection of ideas, inventions, and discoveries; patentability; securing the patent; amendment and correction of patents; and infringement remedies, defenses, and procedure. 2 to 4 graduate hours. 2 to 3 professional hours.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Income Taxation
courses.description: The fundamental course in federal income taxation. Includes materials relating to income taxation of individuals and an introduction to taxation of corporations and shareholders. 4 graduate hours. 3 or 4 professional hours.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Corporate Taxation
courses.description: In-depth study of federal income tax law related to taxation of corporations, shareholders, partnerships, and partners. 4 graduate hours. 3 professional hours.
courses.prereqText: LAW 647.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Partnership Taxation
courses.description: Involves the study of Subchapter K of the Internal Revenue Code, including partnership formation, allocations, distributions, and liquidations. Also examines the tax treatment of Subchapter S corporations. 4 graduate hours. 3 professional hours.
courses.prereqText: LAW 647.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Tax Exempt Organizations
courses.description: Covers the rationale and technical tax requirements for exempting charities from federal and state taxes. Subjects will include the rationale for exemption (especially with respect to churches, schools, and hospitals), qualification rules under I.R.C. Section 5 (c) (3), the Unrelated Business Income Tax, and if time permits, the charitable contributions deduction. 4 graduate hours. 3 professional hours.
courses.prereqText: LAW 647 is a prerequisite, though it may be waived in appropriate cases.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: International Business Trans
courses.description: Doing business abroad: export-import regulations, use of foreign commission merchants, licensing of patents and know-how, investment and exchange problems, establishing a foreign operation (including forms of business organization available abroad), and application of United States and foreign antitrust law to the business operation. 4 graduate hours. 3 professional hours.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: International Trade Policy
courses.description: Analysis of the regulation of trade between nations by international agreement (e.g., the GATT), by multinational organizations (e.g., the European Communities), and by individual countries; emphasizes U.S. import restraints, export controls, and related laws. 4 graduate hours. 3 professional hours.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: European Union Law
courses.description: Intensive study of the European Common Market, particularly of its laws relating to trade barriers, establishment of companies, and antitrust; and United States legislation in the field of international trade. 2 to 4 graduate hours. 2 to 3 professional hours.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: International Law
courses.description: The nature, sources, and subjects of international law and its place in the control of international society; includes an examination of the law of jurisdiction, territory, recognition and succession of states, rights and immunities of states in foreign courts, diplomatic immunities, treaties, protection of citizens abroad, settlement of international disputes, war and neutrality, the United Nations, and the International Court of Justice. 4 graduate hours. 3 professional hours.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: International Human Rights Law
courses.description: Studies established and developing legal rules and procedures governing the protection of international human rights, including Marxist and Third World, as well as Western, conceptions of those rights. 4 graduate hours. 3 professional hours.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Individual Employee Rights
courses.description: This course investigates the legal rights and responsibilities of employees in the non-union workplace. The course will emphasize particularly the role of law in adjusting the balance of power between individual employees and employers. It will study the regulation of contract, tort, and statute of such areas as hiring, discharge, compensation, employee privacy and dignity and the like. 4 graduate hours. 3 professional hours.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Labor Law I
courses.description: Study of the National Labor Relations Act as amended, the pre-act history of the labor movement, and the judiciary's response thereto, with emphasis on understanding the problems, experiments, and forces leading to the enactment; includes the negotiation and administration of the collective bargaining agreement, especially the grievance arbitration procedure, its operation and place in national labor policy; and explores the relationship of the individual and the union. Same as LER 547. 4 graduate hours. 3 or 4 professional hours.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Employment Discrimination
courses.description: Problems arising under federal statutory prohibitions of discrimination in employment, with particular emphasis on evidentiary problems and the use of statistical proofs; defining relevant labor pools, using statistical analyses of data, and establishing proof of test validation. 2 or 4 graduate hours. 2 to 3 professional hours.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Family Law
courses.description: The creation and dissolution of the family, and legal relationships established by marriage, cohabitation and procreation. Covers the law of marriage, divorce, annulment, separation, unmarried cohabitation, illegitimacy, adoption and rights of child custody, parental property on divorce, inheritance, and related rights. Legal rules are placed into the social setting in which they operate, and emphasis is given to family policy as reflected in current developments in family law reform, including constitutional law. 4 graduate hours. 3 professional hours.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Decedents' Estates and Trusts
courses.description: Studies the means of transferring wealth, with primary emphasis on gratuitous transfers; the means available for making gratuitous transfers, including the validity and effect of testamentary instruments and trust deeds; and problems concerning the dispositive provisions of any type of instrument which transfers wealth. 4 graduate hours. 3 professional hours.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Elder Law
courses.description: Examines the various legal implications of people living longer, with special emphasis on public policies and programs affecting the financing of medical care, housing arrangements, and income maintenance of persons aged 60 years and older. 4 graduate hours. 3 professional hours.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Workers Compensation
courses.description: A general survey class on rules relating to workers compensation claims and litigation. Begins with an overview of the historical development of workers compensation laws, then surveys the general principles applicable to such laws, with particular emphasis on the Illinois Workers Compensation Act. Guest speakers will include an arbitrator, a petitioner's attorney, and a claims manager. 3 graduate hours. 2 professional hours.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Products Liability
courses.description: Substantive theories of products liability: negligence, breach of warranty, strict liability, and tortious misrepresentation; procedural and remedial problems with, and defenses to, each substantive theory. 2 to 4 graduate hours. 2 to 3 professional hours.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Insurance Law
courses.description: Covers principles generally applicable to insurance law and includes distinctive rules governing certain types of insurance coverage; objectives are to examine the nature of the insurance contract, marketing of insurance, principles of indemnity, individuals and entities protected by insurance rules, and risks that are shifted by insurance coverage. 4 graduate hours. 3 professional hours.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Anthropology and Law
courses.description: Introduction to the field of legal anthropology. Addresses anthropological theories of the nature of law and disputes, examines related studies of legal structures in non-Western cultures, and considers the uses of anthropology in studying facets of our own legal system. 4 graduate hours. 3 professional hours.
courses.prereqText: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Criminal Proc: Adjudication
courses.description: Problems in the administration of criminal justice, with emphasis upon the commencement of formal proceedings (bail, decision to prosecute, grand jury, preliminary hearing, location of prosecution, scope of prosecution, speedy trial); the adversary system (pleas, discovery, jury trials, prejudicial publicity, ethical problems, double jeopardy); and post-conviction review (post-trial motions, appeals, habeas corpus, related post-conviction remedies). 4 graduate hours. 3 professional hours.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Professional Responsibility
courses.description: Problem course analyzing ethical issues that arise in the practice of law and considering the approaches to such issues taken by the American Bar Association's Code of Professional Responsibility, Model Rules of Professional Conduct, and Code of Judicial Conduct. 2 to 4 graduate hours. 2 to 3 professional hours.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Evidence
courses.description: Law governing the proof of disputed issues of fact; function of the court and jury; competence and examination of witnesses; standards of relevancy; privileged communications; illegal evidence; hearsay rule; best evidence rule; presumptions; and judicial notice. 4 graduate hours. 3 or 4 professional hours.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Complex Litigation
courses.description: Legal and practical issues in "complex" cases: problems of joinder in multi-party cases, consolidation of cases brought independently (including the activities of the Judicial Panel of Multidistrict Litigation), class actions, discovery issues including the assertion and waiver of evidentiary privileges and use of computers, consequences of active judicial "management" of litigation at the pretrial stage, settlement of complex cases, and res judicata problems. 4 graduate hours.3 professional hours.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Federal Courts
courses.description: Examination of the relationship of federal courts to other organs of federal government and to the states, including an analysis of cases dealing with congressional control over jurisdiction, federal review of state court decisions (including the relationship between state and federal substantive and procedural law), and application of law to fact; the scope of the federal question of jurisdiction in federal courts; abstention; federal injunctions of state criminal proceedings; and problems of justiciability, advisory opinions, and mootness. 4 graduate hours. 3 professional hours.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Dispute Resolution
courses.description: Examination of the limitations, consequences, and costs, as well as the indispensability of some aspects of modern litigation; the possibilities, requirements, and legal problems of consensual and of court-annexed dispute resolution processes alternative to final judicial adjudication, including legal counseling, negotiation, mediation, arbitration, mini-trials, summary trials, summary jury trials, early neutral evaluation, private resolution providers, and settlement processes; current disputes used for illustration. 2 to 4 graduate hours. 2 to 3 professional hours.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Remedies
courses.description: Survey of legal and equitable remedies for the protection of personal and property rights. Procedural and substantive aspects of injunctions; restitution of unjust enrichment in the context of the receipt of unsolicited benefits, benefits derived from the commission of tortious acts, and the mistaken acquisition of benefits; alternative remedies arising from bargain transactions; and remedies for violations of civil rights. 2 or 4 graduate hours. 2 to 3 professional hours.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Jurisprudence
courses.description: The place of law in society; the nature, goals, and methods of law; and the relation of law and social science. 4 graduate hours. 3 professional hours.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: American Legal History
courses.description: Studies selected topics in the development of law and legal institutions in the United States with particular emphasis on the history of the legal profession, legal education, and the role of lawyers and courts in U.S. society. 4 graduate hours. 3 professional hours.
courses.prereqText: Some prior study of U.S. history, particularly social and intellectual, is helpful but not required.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Law and Economics
courses.description: Introduction to the economic analysis of law, including property, contracts, torts, criminal law, and related topics. 4 graduate hours. 3 professional hours.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Field Placements
courses.description: Several field placements offer practical legal education, through field work in various agencies. Students engage in legal work under the supervision of experiences attorneys; the work may include conducting client interviews, doing legal research and fact investigation, preparing legal documents, negotiating, and in some cases, engaging in real trials. 1 to 5 professional hours. Approved for both Letter and S/U grading. May be repeated in the same term up to 15 professional hours or in separate terms up to 40 professional hours.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Clinical Training
courses.description: Several clinics offer practical legal education through a variety of in-house clinics. The clinics focus on specific lawyering skills that are relevant to a particular area of practice (e.g., litigation or family advocacy), and have a classroom component. Students engage in legal work under the supervision of experienced attorneys; the work may include conducting client interviews, doing legal research and fact investigation, preparing legal documents, negotiating, and in some cases, engaging in real trials. 1 to 5 graduate hours. 1 to 5 professional hours. Approved for Letter and S/U grading. May be repeated for up to 12 graduate or professional hours if topics vary.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Trial Advocacy
courses.description: Examination of the problems of advocacy and tactics at the trial level. Students engage in all aspects of actual trial work, including witness preparation, opening and closing statements, direct and cross examination, and jury instructions; culminates in student conduct of a full jury trial in late spring; demonstrations are conducted by staff and visiting judges and practitioners. 2 to 3 graduate hours. 2 to 4 professional hours. Approved for Letter and S/U grading. May be repeated, if topics vary.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Fundamentals of Trial Practice
courses.description: Explores the theory and reality of trial practice, from developing a theory of the case through submission of jury instructions; topics include fact gathering, jury selection, opening statements, direct and cross-examination, exhibits, expert witnesses, and closing arguments. 3 professional hours. 4 graduate hours. Approved for both letter and S/U grading.
courses.prereqText: LAW 694 and completion or concurrent enrollment in LAW 682.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Legal Problems
courses.description: Preparation of articles and notes for publication in the University of Illinois Law Review, Elder Law Journal, Journal of Law Technology and Policy, Illinois Law Update section of the Illinois Bar Journal. Teaching practicums and clinical assistantships for Law courses and clinics. 1 to 2 professional hours. Approved for letter and S/U grading. May be repeated to a maximum of 8 hours in the same term and to a maximum of 22 hours in separate terms.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Moot Court
courses.description: Preparation of an appellate brief; presentation of an appellate oral argument; participation in intramural, state, national, or international moot court competition. 1 to 3 graduate hours. 1 to 2 professional hours. Approved for S/U grading only. May be repeated.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Individual research on a special problem selected in consultation with the instructor. 0 to 2 graduate hours. 0 to 2 professional hours. Approved for letter and S/U grading. May be repeated to a maximum of 2 hours.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Leadership Project
courses.description: Course carries no academic credit, but recognizes law students who participate in a prescribed number of lectures, book review session, seminars, and classes relating to principles of leadership. Participation in these activities may be performed at any time during the student’s three years of law school, and must be documented through reports to the Director of the Leadership Project. 0 graduate hours. 0 professional hours. Approved for S/U grading only.
courses.prereqText: Students may enroll only with permission of the Director of the Leadership Project. Enrollment in the J.D. or LL.M. program at the College of Law.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Current Legal Problems
courses.description: This is an umbrella course listing for specialty topics of current legal issues of interest. Additional fees may apply. See Class Schedule. 2 to 4 graduate hours. 1 to 4 professional hours. Approved for letter and S/U grading. May be repeated.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Advanced Litigation Topics
courses.description: This is an umbrella course listing for specialty topics of current interest in litigation. 1 to 4 graduate hours. 1 to 4 professional hours. Approved for letter and S/U grading. May be repeated if topics vary.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Adv Topics in Business Law
courses.description: This is an umbrella course listing in business law for specialty topics of current interest. 1 to 4 graduate hours. 1 to 4 professional hours. Approved for letter and S/U grading. May be repeated if topics vary.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Adv Topics in Criminal Law
courses.description: This is an umbrella course listing in criminal law for specialty topics of current interest. 1 to 4 graduate hours. 1 to 4 professional hours. May be repeated if topics vary.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Comparative Law Topics
courses.description: This is an umbrella course listing in comparative law for specialty topics of current interest. 1 to 4 graduate hours. 1 to 4 professional hours. Approved for letter and S/U grading. May be repeated if topics vary.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Intellectual Property Topics
courses.description: This is an umbrella course listing in intellectual property law for specialty topics of current interest. 1 to 4 graduate hours. 1 to 4 professional hours. Approved for Letter and S/U grading. May be repeated if topics vary.

courses.subject: LAW
courses.title: Seminars
courses.description: This is an umbrella course listing for specialty topics of special interest. Approved for professional and graduate credit. May be repeated.
